subject: Demo recap + proposed acceptance criteria & sprint plan — Sierra Digital POC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@sierra-digital.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sierra-digital.com>
Cc: kdiv_reps@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed sprint plan for POC (next steps)

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a proposed POC approach so we keep momentum while your team aligns on priorities.

Demo highlights (2-minute recap):
- Inference pipeline: low-latency scoring + prefix/KV caching reduced median latency by ~30% in the demo workload.
- Security: VPC & customer-managed KMS discussed (you indicated this is a must for audit).
- Integrations: S3 ingestion path + webhook outputs for downstream DSP.

Proposed POC objectives (what success looks like):
1) Throughput: sustained 150 requests/minute with p95 latency < 250ms across the 1–2k token range.
2) Cost: measured per-token cost below your current baseline by at least 25% (same quality).
3) Quality: parity against your current system on our shared eval set (F1 >= 0.88 on entity extraction).
4) Security/compliance: demonstration of audit log exports and KMS key rotation in your VPC.

Attached is a short sprint plan that maps ownership, milestones, and acceptance criteria: Sierra_POC_SprintPlan_v1.0.pdf (high level, 4 weeks). Key owners we suggest:
- Redwood AE: Evelyn Hart (me) — overall coordination, weekly syncs
- Redwood Solutions Engineer: Karthik Iyer — onboarding and infra setup
- Sierra Tech Lead: Tom Reynolds — testdata, infra access
- Sierra Security: Alicia Gomez — compliance sign-off

Immediate next steps (please confirm by EOD Tue):
- Can you confirm the two eval datasets we discussed (sample sizes listed on page 2 of the attached)?
- Is procurement comfortable with a 30-day SOW / trial? If not, what cadence do you prefer for procurement review?
- Proposed kickoff slot: Wed 21 Apr 10–11am PT — suggest a 60-min technical kick-off + access checklist.

If that works I’ll schedule the kickoff, share a runbook, and loop Karthik for infra prep.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com | M: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Sierra_POC_SprintPlan_v1.0.pdf (11 pages)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@sierra-digital.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sierra-digital.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@sierra-digital.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed sprint plan for POC (next steps)

Thanks, Evelyn — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The security objective is top priority for us. We need to validate audit logs and KMS integration during the POC; please include a sample of the audit log format (JSON fields) in the runbook.
- For quality acceptance, we will run two evaluation slices: (a) entity extraction on 5k records, (b) paraphrase detection on 1k pairs. Can you confirm the expected compute footprint for those runs?
- Procurement: we prefer a 30-day trial but procurement will request a short SOW and an MSA addendum. I’ve CC’d procurement to start the paperwork conversation.

Tom and I are OK with the proposed kickoff window on Wed 21 Apr 10–11am PT — provisional on procurement reviewing SOW.

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director, Security & Compliance | Sierra Digital
E: alicia.gomez@sierra-digital.com

Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed sprint plan for POC (next steps)

Appreciate the quick reply, Alicia. I’ve expanded the sprint plan and added an SLA matrix (attached) and a short checklist that shows what we need from Sierra to kick off. Details below.

Compute footprint estimate for eval runs (ballpark):
- Entity extraction (5k records): 1 x n1-standard (8 vCPU / 32GB) for ~3 hours or 2 smaller instances in parallel to reduce wall time.
- Paraphrase batch (1k pairs): can be run within the same instance, ~45–60 minutes.
- We’ll provide a cost estimate in the runbook; exact numbers depend on batch size and quantization profile.

Security/runbook items added:
- Sample audit log JSON (fields: timestamp, request_id, model_name, input_len, output_len, action, user_id) included in POC-Checklist.md.
- KMS flow diagram and required IAM roles added to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSD-POC-DriveLink

Revised timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (prep, 2–3 days): infra access, test data transfer, service account & KMS test key, baseline run.
- Week 1 (validation): run eval slices + initial performance tuning.
- Week 2 (optimization): batching, KV caching, quantization experiments.
- Week 3 (acceptance): run acceptance tests, compile results, review + sign-off.

Next steps I will take this afternoon:
- Share the updated package (Sierra_POC_SprintPlan_v1.1.pdf) and SLA_matrix.xlsx to the Drive link and attach the POC-Checklist.md to this thread.
- Schedule kickoff for Wed 21 Apr 10–11am PT (tentative) — will invite Karthik as SE and Monica for success metrics tracking.

Karthik / Monica — can you confirm availability for Wed 21 Apr 10–11am PT? Also call out any infrastructure restrictions we should know about (VPN, IP allowlist, firewall).

Best,
Evelyn

Attachments: SLA_matrix.xlsx; POC-Checklist.md
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sierra-digital.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed sprint plan for POC (next steps)

Thanks, Evelyn — all good from engineering. Wed 21 Apr at 10am PT works for our team (I’ll be on the call). Procurement is starting a short SOW draft and will push through any data-protection clauses they need.

Two quick asks from our side before kickoff:
- Please confirm who will own the run of the acceptance evaluation (Redwood or Sierra) and the exact Docker image or endpoint to use.
- Can you list any sample IP ranges we need to allow for the initial infra test?

I’ll circulate the procurement SOW internally and aim to have comments by Tue EOD.

Tom
